text:
maria: Heads up — since 03:10 UTC we're seeing intermittent DNS failures for model-fetch in ap-northeast-1 edge pool. Batch jobs hang on model download with "no such host" for s3-internal.redwood.local.

 dan: Can you paste the node /etc/resolv.conf and a quick dig from a failing pod? Also which GPU pool IDs?

 maria: Pool: edge-gpu-apne1-batch-2. /etc/resolv.conf from one node:
```
search redwood.internal svc.cluster.local
nameserver 10.0.0.2
nameserver 172.31.2.5
options ndots:5 rotate
```
Dig from inside pod (shortened):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> s3-internal.redwood.local @10.0.0.2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; ANSWER SECTION:
s3-internal.redwood.local. 60 IN A 10.200.8.9
;; Query time: 4 msec
```

 linh: That's returning an internal IP (10.200.8.9) — expected for split-horizon. But nodes in that subnet don't have routing to 10.200.8.0/24 (that's behind the storage VPC). Should be hitting the apex public LB instead.

 alex: We're also seeing conntrack port exhaustion on the same hosts around the same time window. Example from klog:
```
nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet.
```
If DNS points to an internal IP the node tries to TCP connect and eventually exhausts ephemeral ports for retries.

 maria: stack trace in the downloader shows repeated SYN timeouts then "dial tcp: i/o timeout". Some pods eventually fallback to HTTPS over proxy and succeed.

 dan: Two simultaneous issues then: (1) split-horizon answer with internal IP that isn't routable from edge nodes, (2) heavy retry pattern causing local port churn. Any recent changes to edge resolver config or the split-horizon zone? @ops-bot did we push anything to infra-dns this morning?

 ops-bot: deploy:infra-dns #2319 applied to prod zones at 02:45 UTC — added conditional view for s3-internal to return private IP for corp VPCs.

 linh: That change inadvertently included apne1 edge pool CIDRs in the allowed list due to an overlapping prefix (10.200.0.0/16). It should have been 10.200.128.0/25 only. So apne1 nodes match and get private answers.

 alex: Temporary mitigation: add a daemonset that writes /etc/hosts with the public LB IP for s3-internal.redwood.local on affected GPU nodes. Quick, but ugly.

 maria: I put up a quick patch to infra-daemonset: mounts /etc/hosts and appends mapping to public IP 54.210.33.11 for s3-internal.redwood.local. Rolling to 4 nodes now.

 dan: Also bumping net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range and conntrack_max on those hosts to reduce immediate failures. PR to infra-kube-node: #549.

 linh: Long term fix: revert the overly-broad split-horizon change and restrict it back to the intended prefix. I've opened infra-dns PR #2322 to tighten the ACL and add unit tests for prefix overlap. Will coordinate rollback if hosts still misbehaving after the daemonset.

 alex: Can we also change resolv.conf options to include "options timeout:1 single-request" on the edge image? Reduce retry time and avoid long SYN storms. We'll test on canary nodes.

 maria: Monitoring: added dashboard widgets for DNS answer IPs for s3-internal, conntrack usage, and kube-proxy conntrack miss rates. Alerts set for >70% conntrack and >5% fwd failures.

 dan: Plan: 1) finish daemonset hotfix to all impacted pools (15m) 2) apply conntrack tweaks (10m) 3) merge infra-dns tighten (after CI) and safely roll out with canary (30m) 4) revert daemonset once DNS fixed. Postmortem if reoccur.

 linh: Filing incident runbook entry and tagging for postmortem. Incident-ops: assigning to maria/dan/linh. :white_check_mark:

 maria: Thanks — I'll watch the rollout and update when the batch queue drain completes. If anyone sees more "no such host" pings in apne1 drop a line here.
